top_signals.title: Fighting Spreads Across Ethiopia as Conflict Fears Mount
top_signals.summary: Flights were suspended and internet services disrupted across parts of northern Ethiopia as fighting spread and the government said it had killed 272 rebels, raising fears of a return to the brutal civil war that ended in 2022.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: North Korea’s Irregular Warfare After Ukraine
top_signals.summary:
Pyongyang has a long history of conducting irregular warfare and asymmetric operations: Look no further than the 1968 Blue House raid or the 1996 submarine incursion as the most pressing examples. More often than not, North Korea failed to achieve the intended objectives of its missions and lost its commandos. Despite failures, the regime pressed on, and now, over thirty years after the sub incursion, it has the combat experience of its special operations forces in Kursk to leverage. top_signals.title: Dollar’s Best Rally Since March Is Set to Last as Fortunes Shift
top_signals.summary: The dollar is headed for its best two-week stretch in six months in a reversal of fortunes that’s likely to support the currency through the rest of the year, asset managers and strategists say.

top_signals.title: Hormuz Tanker Transits Crash to Single Digits as Crisis Deepens
top_signals.summary: Only nine commodity carriers passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, eight of them exiting the waterway, Reuters reported in its now regular update on tanker numbers in the strait. The Thursday total is a further decline on already depressed numbers that have now gone from double to single digits, with the 10-day average at 18.
